System

Fixed camera, zoom, depth and occluder handling

Use a fixed three-quarter camera that follows the local pawn with clamped zoom. The camera is local presentation: it does not rotate collision, change server movement axes or confer visibility permission for attacks through walls.

Scope and player interaction

Use a fixed three-quarter camera that follows the local pawn with clamped zoom. The camera is local presentation: it does not rotate collision, change server movement axes or confer visibility permission for attacks through walls.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase01committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Unpossessed → Following → Zooming → OccluderFaded → TravelScreen → Preview

WBP_Options observes results from URPGCameraComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Camera_Default. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
AzimuthDegrees=45 and ElevationDegrees=50; defaults, not free player rotation
FieldOfViewDegrees=35 for first perspective trial
ArmLengthCm: clamped 900..1600; zoom steps or analog wheel input
FollowLagSeconds: optional small local interpolation; no server position smoothing duplication
OcclusionCandidateTags: only authored environmental occluders
OpacityMinimum=0.25 and FadeSeconds=0.15; cosmetic proposal

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGCameraComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_OptionsLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
SetZoomIntent(Value) -> ClampedZoom; client-only
BindFollowTarget(Pawn) -> Following|Unpossessed; local possession observer
UpdateOccluders(CameraToPawnSegment) -> LocalFadeSet; client-only traces
RestoreOccluders() -> Cleared; on travel, destruction, options change

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Local controller binds the camera to its currently possessed pawn, not PlayerController index 0 in shared server code.
  2. Zoom input modifies the clamped local camera arm; fixed azimuth/elevation remain stable across facing changes.
  3. Camera obstruction checks collect only tagged visual occluders between camera and avatar. Maintain reference counts when several traces request a fade.
  4. Create per-client dynamic material instances or an explicitly client-local visibility solution; do not modify shared material assets or server collision.
  5. When the actor is no longer an occluder, restore its original material parameters; teardown also restores everything.
  6. Compare perspective and orthographic screenshots at identical apparent avatar size on slopes/bridges before choosing a projection; record results rather than declaring a universal winner.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Add a SpringArm and Camera under a stable camera root, separate from VisualRoot. Disable inherited control rotation and collision-driven facing rotation of the camera.
  2. Assign DA_Camera_Default in BP_PlayerCharacter or the local controller camera adapter; tune FOV/arm length in L_ArtLab, not on a production biome first.
  3. Create M_OccluderFade and MI_OccluderFade_Test with a local opacity parameter; use on a limited test wall/tree canopy before broader materials.
  4. Bind IA_Zoom to SetZoomIntent and remove all camera rotation mappings. Add a zoom slider to WBP_Options with the same clamp.
  5. Reopen all tagged occluder actors after material changes; verify camera fade does not disable weapon LOS or world collision.

Reopen Phase01 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_ArtLab / NearWall / TreeCanopy / RaisedBridge. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Two clients look through the same tree from different positions -> each has its own fade result, unchanged server collision.
Camera pawn destroyed during fade -> originals restored and no dangling material references.
Zoom to extremes -> no black borders, lost foot anchor or unacceptable sprite shimmer; clamp/tune on failure.
Enemy behind opaque wall -> soft target may show UI policy, but server attack LOS still rejects.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Perspective settings are trial values, not art-calibrated recommendations. Orthographic fallback must pass sorting, scale, shadow and height readability tests before adoption.

Log only changed occluder sets in development. Camera shake, motion reduction, follow lag and zoom sensitivity are accessibility options; no network RPC per camera frame.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
